paper.title: Tabular Deep Learning vs Classical Machine Learning for Urban Land Cover Classification (arXiv 2609.19010)
paper.note: Not committed; pass the downloaded PDF as the second argument. Its SHA-256 must match.

claim.location: Table 2, row Random Forest, test accuracy column

repository.why: The paper's code repository; its notebook trains the Random Forest of Table 2.

notes: The repository's requirements.txt is unpinned; these are the pins of the project's reviewed Urban Land Cover case.

expected.why: The notebook is run through a project-owned adapter (status capped at partially_reproduced), and the paper's protocol differs from the notebook in four documented ways. The run is not required to match the paper: not_reproduced, or partially_reproduced within the 1.0 pp tolerance, are both acceptable outcomes. The expected observed value is deliberately not recorded here.

caveats: The adapter fixes the validation split seed to 42; the notebook leaves it unset, so the authors' exact split is unknown.
The secondary metrics (precision, recall, F1, AUC) are recorded by the adapter but not compared.

paperAnalyst.summary: Table 2 reports per-model test results on the UCI Urban Land Cover test set; the Random Forest reaches 81.66% accuracy.

review.summary: The reviewed project-owned adapter ran the notebook's Random Forest protocol on the official CSVs; the accuracy came from the run's own JSON artifact.
concerns: seed fixed to 42 where the notebook leaves it unset
validation split not stratified and test set z-scored independently, unlike the paper's description
